questions.question: In March 2023, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) amended the 2015 PFRDA Regulation to increase the age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 to _______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**70**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In March 2023, the** Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** amended the 2015 PFRDA Regulation to increase the age limit for the Ombudsman from **65 to 70 years.**
 
• Under the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Redressal of Subscriber Grievance) Regulations 2015, the maximum age limit for Ombudsman was set at 65 years.
 
• However, a recent gazette notification dated 27 March announced an amendment by the PFRDA, changing the upper age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 to 70 years.
 
• The Ombudsman, appointed by PFRDA, is tasked with receiving, assessing, and facilitating the resolution of complaints or grievances falling under the regulations.
 
• An individual selected as an Ombudsman serves a term of three years and may be considered for reappointment for an additional two years. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) **serves as the regulatory authority overseeing pensions in India, operating within the purview of the Ministry of Finance under the Government of India.
 
• Its establishment in 2003 stemmed from the recommendations outlined in the OASIS report commissioned by the Indian government, coinciding with the inception of the Indian National Pension Scheme.

questions.question: How many members are nominated by the President in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __12__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• **Twelve members are nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President of India for the six-years terms **for their contributions towards arts, literature, sciences, and social services.

 
 
• This right has been bestowed upon the President according to the Fourth Schedule (Articles 4(1) and 80(2)) of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• Unlike the members of the Lok Sabha, the membership of the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved at any time.
 
 
• However, every second year, one-third of the members retire and at the beginning of every third year, the vacancies are filled by fresh elections and the nomination of the President__.
 
• A Member of Parliament (abbreviated: MP) in the Rajya Sabha is the representative of the Indian states to one of the two houses of the Parliament of India (Rajya Sabha).
 
• Rajya Sabha MPs are elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of the State Legislative Assembly with a system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] __Additional Information__ 

 
• The representatives of the states and union territories in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the method of indirect election.
 
 
• The representatives of each State and the two Union Territories are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of that State and the members of the electoral college for that Union Territory, as the case may be, in accordance with the system of proportional representation. Instruments of single transferable vote.
 
• The Electoral College for the National Capital Territory of Delhi consists of the elected members of the Delhi Legislative Assembly, and for Puducherry the elected members of the Puducherry Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• Special Powers of Rajya Sabha
 
 
• The Upper House also has some special powers, such as:
 
 
• Power to transfer a subject from the State List to the Union List for a specified period (Article 249).
 
• To create additional All India Services (Article 312).
 
• To support emergency under Article 352 for a limited period when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.​

questions.question: ______ holds office from the date of his/her election till immediately before the first meeting of the Lok Sabha after the dissolution of the one to which he/she was elected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The speaker of the Lok Sabha/legislative assembly vacates the office immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected house.
 
• After a general election and the formation of a newly elected house, a pro-tem or interim speaker is appointed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pro-tem is a Latin phrase that means **“for the time being”.**
 
• President/governor appoints the pro-tem speaker to preside over the sittings of the newly elected house.
 
• Usually, the **senior-most member** of the house is made the pro-tem speaker.
 
• The first meeting after the election when the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are selected by members of the Parliament is held under the pro tem Speaker.
 
• The pro tem Speaker also administers the oath of office to the newly elected MPs.
 
• On the election of a new Speaker, the office of the pro tem speaker ceases to exist.
 
• The **Vice President** holds office for **five years**. The Vice President can be re-elected any number of times. However, the office may be terminated earlier by death, resignation, or removal. The Constitution does not provide a mechanism of succession to the office of Vice President in the event of an extraordinary vacancy, apart from re-election. However, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can perform the Vice President's duties as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha in such an event.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 61.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 61 of the Constitution of India prescribes the procedure for the impeachment of the President.**
 
• When the President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by either House of Parliament.
 
• The president may also be removed before the expiry of the term through impeachment for violating the Constitution of India by the Parliament of India. 
 
• The process may start in either of the two houses of the parliament.
 
• The house initiates the process by leveling the charges against the president.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Process of Impeachment:**

 
 
• ​After the House of Representatives sends its articles of impeachment to the Senate, the Senate sits as a High Court of Impeachment to consider evidence, hear witnesses, and vote to acquit or convict the impeached official. A committee of representatives, called “managers,” act as prosecutors before the Senate.
 
 
 
• ​The President, Vice President, and all civil Officers of the United States shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors.
 
• Meaning of Impeachment:
 
• To charge with a crime or misconduct specifically: to charge (a public official) before a competent tribunal (as the U.S. Senate) with misconduct in office. Note: Impeachment is the first step in removing an officer from office.

questions.question: Who has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power to regulate the right of citizenship in India is vested in the **Parliament**.
 
• According to the Constitution of India, the Parliament has the authority to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters related to citizenship.
 
• Article 11 of the Indian Constitution grants Parliament the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• Over the years, Parliament has enacted several laws to govern citizenship, including the Citizenship Act of 1955.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955** provides for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• The Act has been amended multiple times, with significant amendments in 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, and 2019.
 
• Citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, or incorporation of territory.
 
• The Constitution of India, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, laid the foundation for the legal framework of citizenship in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT** correct regarding the election of Vice-President?

options.text: He/she is qualified for election as a member of the House of People.
He/she is qualified for election as a member of the Council of States.
He/she has completed the age of 35 years of age.
He/she must be a citizen of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He/she is qualified for election as a member of the House of People**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Election of Vice-President**

 
 
• The **Vice-President is elected by an electoral college made up of representatives from both Houses of Parliament **using a single transferable vote under the proportional representation system.
 
• **Voting** in this election is conducted **confidentially**.
 
• All members of **both Houses of Parliament make up the Electoral College, which chooses the Vice-President**.
 
• A candidate cannot win the vice presidential nomination unless –
 
 
• **He/she is qualified for election as a member of the Council of States.**
 
• **He/she has completed the age of 35 years of age.**
 
• **He/she must be a citizen of India.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vice-President is not a **member of the state legislature or of either house of parliament**.
 
• If a **member of either the House of Parliament or the House of the Legislature of any state is elected vice president, he or she is deemed to have resigned from that position** on the day they enter the office. 
 
• When the **President cannot perform his duties because of absence, illness, or any other reason, the Vice-President serves as President until a new President is elected** and is the **ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution mentions that “the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha)”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 79** of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses known respectively as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is the upper house of the Parliament, representing the states and union territories.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of the Parliament, representing the people of India as a whole.
 
• This structure ensures a bicameral legislative system, providing a system of checks and balances within the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

options.text: Rajya Sabha but not in Lok Sabha
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha or any state legislative assembly
Lok Sabha but not in Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:

__
 
• The President may be removed from office before the completion of this term through impeachment for violating the Constitution of India by the Parliament of India.
 
• The process of impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in either house of the parliament and such resolution has to be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House.
 
• Article 61 of the Indian Constitution provides the Procedure for impeachment of the President Of India.

• **Qualifications of the President are**:

 
 
• He should be an Indian Citizen
 
• His age should be a minimum of 35 years
 
• He should qualify the conditions to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha
 
• He should not hold any office of profit under the central government, state government, or any public authority.
 
 
 
• The President is elected indirectly by members of an electoral college consisting of:
 
 
• the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament;
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states;
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
